page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 123.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing approximately 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 3890 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, rank in the top 10% of tested servers. The Passmark memory score also places in the top tier. However, multi-core performance and database operations, including Redis SET and static web serving throughput, fall into the average tier. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory write bandwidth for large uncached blocks, which is classified in the bottom 25% at 21.85 GB/sec, contrasting with the average read bandwidth of 45.62 GB/sec.

The server demonstrates strong capabilities for lightweight LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds of 423.0 tokens/sec with a small 135M model, though performance scales down to average levels for medium 7B models. Given the combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing, high-capacity DDR5 memory, and substantial local NVMe storage, this hardware profile offers high resource density without the overhead of virtualization. It is well-suited for single-threaded intensive tasks, local database hosting, caching layers, and web serving workloads that benefit from fast local storage and high single-core efficiency.
